messages:
Mia (eng-platform): quick sanity check — we're about to roll the tiered sampler (route + customer_tier + retention_budget). main concerns: correctness for long traces, exporter backpressure, console rollout UX. any red flags?
Alex R: main thing is long-running traces getting truncated by tail sampling. head sampling helps but we need stable heuristics for when to switch to tail.
Samir: agree. also watch out for partial spans — if a span is sampled but parent isn't, we should still keep parent context otherwise flamegraphs become noisy.
Rachel (observability): we should emit two metrics: sampled_rate_per_route and dropped_span_count_per_tenant. without them, ops can't tell if sampler misbehaved.
Julian (eng-sre): exporter backpressure: if exporter returns 429 or OOM, sampler should temporarily increase tail sampling to reduce volume. flow: detect backpressure -> increase drop rate -> notify.
Priya: UX note — console rollout needs dry-run + preview mode that shows estimated retention impact per-tenant before commit. customers will ask "how many traces will I lose?"
Mia (eng-platform): good — thinking of API shape: accept config at route level, with fallback to tier and global. payload idea: {"route":"/v1/generate","tiers":{...},"retention_budget":...}. thoughts on storing tenant_id in span? hashed?
Samir: hash tenant_id at source, include as attribute tenant.hash to avoid PII leaks. also add sampling_hint attribute so downstream exporters can decide.
Alex R: small nit: sampling_hint needs stable semantics. propose values: "force_keep", "force_drop", "candidate_head". keep as string enum.
Rachel (observability): add trace-level tag "sampling.control_version" so we can correlate behavior pre/post rollout. makes debugging much easier.
Mia (eng-platform): example config I'm prototyping:
```yaml
sampler:
  default: tail
  routes:
    /v1/generate:
      tiers:
        enterprise: { head: 0.7, tail: 0.02 }
        standard: { head: 0.15, tail: 0.005 }
  retention_budget_per_tenant: 20000
  on_backpressure: increase_tail_by: 2x
```
Julian (eng-sre): for testing, we should simulate long-running sessions and cross-route traces. also test mis-attributed tenant IDs (race conditions when header missing).
Priya: rollout plan: 1) dry-run for 48h showing metrics, 2) 10% traffic with canary, 3) expand by tier (enterprise first), 4) monitor sampled_rate_per_route and error budget.
Samir: edge-case: client-side retries can explode head-sampling counts. need dedupe window or request-id folding before sampling decision.
Alex R: yes — canonical request_id header should be accepted by sampler. if missing, fallback to span.trace_id.
Rachel (observability): add alert: if sampled_rate deviates >30% from expected for 10m, auto-rollback canary. also surface top 5 routes with unexpected variance.
Mia (eng-platform): ok actions: Samir -> ensure parent retention when child sampled; Alex -> finalize sampling_hint enum & request_id handling; Rachel -> dashboard + alerts; Julian -> backpressure mitigation tests; Priya -> console dry-run UX copy. I'll assemble RFC and ship to infra by EOD.
InfraBot: deployment scheduled: sampler-config v1.9 -> canary group (10%) at 2025-09-17T02:30Z. :rocket:
Mia (eng-platform): thanks all — feel free to DM me if you find anything else. :thumbsup:
